title: EXPLORING PERSONA-DEPENDENT LLM ALIGNMENT FOR THE MORAL MACHINE EXPERIMENT

bias_targets.methodology: Assigning older (32-75 years old) versus younger (18-21 years old) personas to LLMs and measuring the differences in their moral decisions on the Moral Machine experiment using Average Marginal Component Effect (AMCE) and Moral Decision Distance (MDD).
Comparing the moral dilemma decisions of LLMs when prompted with 'less educated' (high school) versus 'more educated' (PhD) personas.

Assigning male versus female personas to LLMs to evaluate how gender identity influences moral decision-making, including tracking the models' preference for sparing females over males in autonomous driving scenarios.
Prompting LLMs with higher income versus lower income personas and measuring their moral choices, including their preference for sparing higher-status characters over lower-status characters.

Assigning conservative versus progressive personas to LLMs and evaluating how political identity shifts preferences in moral dilemmas (e.g., finding that conservative personas heavily favored characters with higher social status).
Evaluating moral decisions by prompting LLMs with 'very religious' versus 'non-religious' personas and comparing the shifts in decision boundaries to human baselines.
Assigning personas based on Western versus Eastern nationalities to assess cultural variations in LLM responses to the Moral Machine experiment scenarios.
